title: Chapter 4 Quiz 1
description: Storing many values of the same type, and finding each one by its position.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is an **array**?
options: One variable holding a single value
A file kept on disk between runs
A loop that repeats some code
questions.explanation: An array groups data of the same type in reserved areas of RAM. Watch out: a variable holds one value, an array holds many.

questions.question: What is the **index** of an array?
questions.explanation: The index locates each cell of the array.

questions.question: All the elements of an array have the same type.
questions.explanation: That is the difference with a record, whose fields can have different types. Watch out: records can mix types, arrays cannot.

questions.question: An index can be a constant or a variable of integer type.
questions.explanation: Either one can be used to select a cell.

questions.question: What does an array declaration need?
questions.explanation: Name, minimum index, maximum index and data type.

questions.question: Which declaration creates an array of 10 averages (real numbers) numbered 1 to 10?
questions.explanation: The syntax gives the index range between brackets, then ARRAY OF and the type.

questions.question: How many cells does an array [0..9] have?
questions.explanation: Indexes 0 to 9 make 10 cells. Watch out: the last index is 9, but there are 10 cells.

questions.question: How many cells does an array [5..12] have?
questions.explanation: 12 - 5 + 1 = 8. Watch out: 12 - 5 = 7, but both ends count.

questions.question: Array T has the values 12, 7, 30, 4 in cells 1 to 4. Give the value of each expression.
questions.explanation: T[i] is the value in cell i. Watch out: the index is the position of the cell, not the value stored in it.

questions.question: This should store values in an array of 5 cells numbered 1 to 5. One line has an error.
questions.code:
Declare T [1..5] : ARRAY OF integer
Let T[0] ← 8
Let T[5] ← 3
Display(T[5])
questions.explanation: The cells are numbered 1 to 5, so T[0] does not exist. Watch out: many languages start at 0, but this array starts at 1.
